title: Russian Doll Envelopes
statement: Find the maximum number of envelopes that can be nested, with both width and height strictly increasing.
explanation: Sort by width ascending and equal widths by height descending, then find a strictly increasing subsequence of heights.

title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
statement: Count nonnegative integers with no repeated decimal digit and fewer than 10^n.
explanation: Count the one-digit case, then extend each longer number with an unused digit.

title: Largest Divisible Subset
statement: Return a largest subset where for every pair, one value divides the other.
explanation: Sort values and extend a divisible subset ending at each value, storing predecessor links to reconstruct it.

title: Wiggle Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest subsequence whose consecutive differences strictly alternate in sign.
explanation: Track the best lengths ending with an upward or downward difference.

title: Combination Sum IV
statement: Count ordered sequences of positive numbers from nums that sum to target.
explanation: For each total, sum the counts for each number that can be the final element.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
statement: Return the kth smallest element in a matrix whose rows and columns are sorted ascending.
explanation: Binary-search the value range and count matrix entries less than or equal to each midpoint.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
statement: Design a collection supporting insert, remove, and uniformly random retrieval in average O(1) time.
explanation: Store values in an array and map each value to its index; remove by swapping with the final element.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
statement: Design a collection supporting duplicates with average O(1) insert, remove one occurrence, and random retrieval.
explanation: Store all occurrences in an array and track each value's occupied indices in a set.

title: Ransom Note
statement: Determine whether a ransom note can be constructed from letters in a magazine, using each magazine letter at most once.
explanation: Count magazine characters and consume one count for every required note character.

title: Lexicographical Numbers
statement: Return integers from 1 through n in lexicographical order.
explanation: Traverse the implicit decimal-prefix tree, visiting children by appending digits 0 through 9.
